source.quote:
Zxecuttve Orbe?
As an experiment, not as a precedent, in lieu of the orders heretofore usually
issued providing that four hours shall constitute a day's work for all clerks and
other employees of the Federal Government and the Government of the District
of Columbia, in the said District of Columbia, on December 24th and December
31st, it is hereby ordered that the several Executive Departments and Independent
Government Establishments in the District of Columbia, including the Government
Printing Ollice and the Navy Yard and stations, be closed on Saturday, December
26, 1925, and all clerks and other employees in the Federal Service in the District
of Columbia, except those who may for special public reasons be excepted from the
provisionls of this order, or those whose absence from duty would be inconsistent
with the provisions of existing law, are hereby excused from duty on that day.
CALVIN COOLIDGE
December 11, 1J25.
[No. 4354]

Actor: EO 4354 itself. The dossier holds no own-terms record for this order, so the end cites the order's complete held text, which contains the stated day.

research_rationale:
EO 4354 (December 11, 1925, Calvin Coolidge), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan text (jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_4354.txt; archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false) and checked against the page image I rendered from the held PDF ('ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders/PT1-1925-EO-4354.pdf', sha256 98b1a107..., one page; printed heading 'Executive Order', signature 'CALVIN COOLIDGE', 'THE WHITE HOUSE, December 11, 1925.', '[No. 4354]'). The OCR layer is complete; its errors ('Zxecuttve Orbe?' for the heading, 'Ollice' for 'Office', 'provisionls', '1J25' for 1925) and the trailing noise (the printer's imprint at the foot of the page) do not affect the operative words. As an experiment and not as a precedent, and in lieu of the orders usually issued making four hours a day's work on December 24 and December 31, it closes the executive departments and independent establishments in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, on Saturday, December 26, 1925, and excuses federal employees in the District from duty that day, except those excepted for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law. The order gives no half-day on December 24 or December 31; its reference to the usual orders explains what it replaces and commands nothing for those days. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1925-12-26, the only day it governs. A reader who dates cessation to the first day without effect would write 1925-12-27; this claim records 1925-12-26, the day through whose end the order ran, consistent with the owner's inclusive reading of stated dates. Identity: the census register lists EO 4354 with the year only; the date December 11, 1925 and the number come from the scan.

source.quote:
And Whereas the public interest requires that Charles J. James, Chief Appraiser, Office of the Register of Wills and Clerk of the Probate Court, Supreme Court of the District of Columbia, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of two years by Executive Order No. 6030, dated February 17, 1933, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until March 1, 1936:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby further exempt Charles J. James from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until March 1, 1936.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

February 26, 1935.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: EO 6030 is read in full in the registered Office of the Federal Register compilation text (jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_6030.txt; grade official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original true; Proclamations and Executive Orders: Herbert Hoover, vol. II (OFR 1974), printed page 1431, PDF page 660). That text is the OCR layer of the HathiTrust scan recorded in its header (PDF sha256 3bce4d49...); the PDF itself is a Git LFS pointer in this checkout, so the page image was not inspected, and the original confirmation rests on the registered compilation text, which is complete: heading, title, one operative sentence, 'THE WHITE HOUSE, February 17, 1933', 'HERBERT HOOVER' and '[No. 6030]'. The held American Presidency Project transcription (mirror capture; page record heading 'Executive Order 6030—Exemption of Charles J. James from Compulsory Retirement for Age', date 1933-02-17, text_sha256 equal to the held file's) agrees in substance. EO 6030 (February 17, 1933, Herbert Hoover) exempts Charles J. James, chief appraiser of the office of the Register of Wills and clerk of the Probate Court, Supreme Court of the District of Columbia, who 'during the current month, has reached the retirement age', from section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and states that he 'is hereby exempted from the provisions of that section until February 28, 1935.' Identity: number, date, person and title agree across the compilation text, the APP page and the census register.  Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1935-02-28, inclusive. Later orders naming the same employee are held and added to this packet as source-supplement excerpts: EO 6975 (February 26, 1935) recites James as 'exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of two years by Executive Order No. 6030, dated February 17, 1933' and further exempts the employee until March 1, 1936. Each is recorded as a later event on the clause (clauses.csv). Extension reading, decided on the texts: each later order is a new exercise of the section 204 proviso with its own period. None says that the earlier order 'is amended' or alters its date; each recites the earlier exemption as a past grant ('who was exempted ... by Executive Order No. ...') and grants a further exemption for a new period. The strike-and-insert ruling does not apply because nothing is struck or inserted. So this order's own command ended on its own stated date, inclusive (exclusive alternative: ended when that day began), and each later order is recorded as a later event naming the same employee; the employee's exempt status continued without a gap under the later orders. The alternative reading, that the later orders prolonged this order's command, would put its first end at the last later order's stated end (1936-03-01, inclusive); the texts do not support it, because no later order operates on this order's text. The searches below found no further order naming this person after EO 6975. Searches made on 2026-10-28: (1) every census-register title (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) containing 'retire' or 'exempt', for the person's surname and full name; (2) a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts (clause-drafts copies excluded) for the person's name; (3) a citation search of the same texts for this order's number in the forms 'No. N', 'Order N' and 'Orders N'. The machine USC and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. The held texts of EO 7945 (August 4, 1938) and EO 8231 (August 31, 1939) grant further exemptions under section 204 (cited there as 5 U.S.C. 715a), which corroborates that the statutory scheme was still in force through the stated end of every order in this batch (the latest is January 1, 1938).

And Whereas the public interest requires that Joe Smith, a mechanician in the Senate Office Building under the Office of the Architect of the Capitol, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until August 31, 1935;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid statute, I do hereby exempt Joe Smith from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until August 31, 1935.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 6302—Exemption of Clayborn L. Gatewood from Compulsory Retirement for Age; September 30, 1933; APP node 362127; common-crawl capture 2025-12-08T01:43:41Z
source.quote:
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404; 5 U.S.C., sec. 692b), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires: "

And Whereas the public interest requires that Clayborn L. Gatewood, junior mechanic in the House wing of the United States Capitol Building, under the office of the Architect of the Capitol, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until September 30, 1935.

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid statute, I do hereby exempt Clayborn L. Gatewood from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until September 30, 1935.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

September 30, 1933.

source.quote:
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404; 5 U.S.C., sec. 692b), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires: * * * ";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Herman H. B. Meyer, Director, Legislative Reference Service, Library of Congress, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until November 1, 1935;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Herman H. B. Meyer from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until November 1, 1935.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

October 3, 1934.

On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires: * * *";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Charles J. James, Chief Appraiser, Office of the Register of Wills and Clerk of the Probate Court, Supreme Court of the District of Columbia, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of two years by Executive Order No. 6030, dated February 17, 1933, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until March 1, 1936:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby further exempt Charles J. James from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until March 1, 1936.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S.C., sec. 692b), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires: * * *";

The White House,

April 30, 1935.

The strike-and-insert ruling does not apply because nothing is struck or inserted. So this order's own command ended on its own stated date, inclusive (exclusive alternative: ended when that day began), and each later order is recorded as a later event naming the same employee; the employee's exempt status continued without a gap under the later orders. source.page_or_item: Executive Order 7230—Exemption of Davis B. Levis from Compulsory Retirement for Age; November 20, 1935; APP node 362730; wayback capture 2023-09-04T20:34:03Z
source.quote:
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S.C., sec. 715a), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * * ";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Davis B. Levis, vice consul and clerk in the American consulate general at Paris, France, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until December 1, 193G:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Davis B. Levis from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until December 1, 1936.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

November 20, 1935.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Thomas M. Thurston, deputy collector in charge of the Liquidating Division, Office of the Collector of Customs, Treasury Department, New York, New York, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 6899, of November 8, 1934, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until December 1, 1936:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby further exempt Thomas M. Thurston from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until December 1, 1936.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

original_representation.quote:
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S.C., sec. 715a), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Miss Mary G. Wilmarth, chief scientific aid, Geological Survey, Department of the Interior, who, during the month of April 1936, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until May 1, 1937;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Miss Mary G. Wilmarth from the provisions thereof and continue her in the service until May 1, 1937.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

March 11 1936.

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 7385—Exemption of John V. Shea From Compulsory Retirement for Age; June 08, 1936; APP node 355227; common-crawl capture 2025-09-17T21:23:12Z
source.quote:
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S.C., sec. 715a), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *";

And Whereas the public interest requires that John V. Shea, senior clerk, Division of Supply, Treasury Department, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 7072 of June 12, 1935, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until July 1, 1937:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt John V. Shea from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until July 1, 1937.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

June 8, 1936.

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Davis B. Levis, vice consul and clerk in the American consulate general at Paris, France, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 7230 of November 20, 1935, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until December 1, 1937;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Davis B. Levis from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until December 1, 1937.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

November 14, 1936.

WHEREAS section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S.C., sec. 715a.), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *";

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that Charles Earle, gardener's helper, National Park Service, Department of the Interior, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until January 1, 1938;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Charles Earle from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until January 1, 1938.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

THE WHITE HOUSE,

December 31, 1936.
